preparation: Avoid high-dose biotin supplements (more than 5 mg/day) for at least 8 hours before blood collection

faqs.question: What does the Thyroglobulin test measure?
faqs.answer: It measures the level of thyroglobulin protein in your blood to monitor thyroid cancer treatment and detect recurrence.

faqs.question: Is fasting required for the Thyroglobulin test?
faqs.answer: Fasting not required; you can eat and drink normally before the test.

faqs.question: When is the Thyroglobulin test recommended?
faqs.answer: It is done after thyroid surgery or radioactive iodine therapy to monitor treatment success and recurrence.

faqs.question: Can biotin affect my Thyroglobulin test results?
faqs.answer: Yes, high-dose biotin supplements can interfere. Avoid them at least 8 hours before testing.

faqs.question: What do high Thyroglobulin levels mean?
faqs.answer: High levels may indicate remaining thyroid tissue, cancer recurrence, or metastasis.

faqs.question: What do low Thyroglobulin levels indicate?
faqs.answer: Low or undetectable levels suggest effective thyroid cancer treatment and no residual tissue.

faqs.question: Can I take my regular medicines before the test?
faqs.answer: Yes, but inform your doctor about all medications or supplements you’re taking.

faqs.question: How often should I do the Thyroglobulin test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor will decide the frequency, often every 6–12 months after thyroid cancer treatment.<
